title: Kafka observability bridge and intent-aware paging
creator: Ava Mercer
description: Build a lightweight Kafka-based bridge that unifies trace spans, metric series, and structured logs into the observability ingestion tier and instrument an intent-aware paging layer that reduces noise for oncall by correlating alerts with service intent (deploys, rollout events, maintenance windows). Scope: 1) a resilient consumer/transformer that normalizes and forwards traces/metrics/logs to our metrics pipeline (Prometheus remote write / Mimir) and tracing backend; 2) enrichment hooks that attach request intent tags (rollout_id, canary_flag, customer_tier) to spans and metrics; 3) alert correlation rules that suppress or down-prioritize pages when intent indicates non-actionable state; 4) dashboards showing pre/post suppression signal quality and false-suppression audits.
acceptance_criteria: Bridge consumes at least 2k messages/sec sustained in staging without data loss and auto-rebalances on consumer group changes
Span/metric/log enrichment adds intent tags to >=99% of incoming requests for supported services
New paging policy reduces noisy pages for known rollout windows by >=45% in the canary test group without increasing missed-severity incidents
End-to-end observability pipeline latency from Kafka ingestion to dashboard index <= 8s p95 under test load
Documentation (design doc + runbook) published and reviewed, and an automated smoke test in CI validates critical paths
deploy_plan: Phase 1: deploy bridge to staging (non-critical cluster) behind feature flag; run load/latency tests and synthetic traces for two weeks. Phase 2: enable enrichment for a single service (payments-api) with canary suppression rules; monitor false-suppression via audit dashboard for 48h. Phase 3: expand to critical services and flip feature flags gradually with automated rollback on SLO degradation. Finalize with Dedicated/Private deployment checklist and runbook updates.
monitoring_runbook: Primary alerting: Bridge consumer lag > 10,000 for 2m => P0 page
Secondary: enrichment error rate > 0.5% for 10m => triage; do not auto-page unless correlated with elevated latency/error SLOs
Paging suppression check: if suppression reduces pages by >75% for an hour and SLOs unchanged, open investigation for over-suppression
Smoke test: synthetic trace appears in dashboard within 8s p95; if not, fail deployment and rollback
notes: We will use existing Kafka clusters and a minimal JVM consumer to reuse our tracing SDK integrations. Trade-offs: JVM choice simplifies SDK reuse but increases memory footprint; alternative Go consumer evaluated but would require porting enrichment libraries. Chosen path allows faster rollout and leverages existing monitoring agents for GC/latency.
